newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia-Thai authority reports fifth natgas find.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia-Thai authority reports fifth natgas find.

text.p: The Malaysia-Thailand Joint Authority said that its contractors have made a fifth gas discovery in the Joint Development Area off the east coast of peninsula Malaysia and Thailand

Well Bumi-1, which was spudded on July 25, was drilled to a total depth of 9,279 feet to test the potential of the Bumi prospect, east of the Suriya Gas Field in Block A-18, a statement from the authority said.
The well encountered several gas-bearing sands, it said.
Six production tests were conducted at depths ranging fom 3,514 to 7,676 feet.
The tests yielded a combined gas flow rate of 73 million standard cubic feet per day plus 305 barrels per day of condensate measured through choke sizes ranging from 3/8 inches to two inches.
The Bumi-1 Well is about 260 km east of Songkhla, Thailand and 140 km northeast of Kota Bharu, on the east coast of Malaysia.
Block A-18 is operated by Carigali-Triton Operating Co, jointly owned by Dallas-based Triton Energy Ltd and Malaysian state oil company Petronas.
A spokesman at the joint authority said the well is the fifth discovery in the Joint Development Area, which includes not only Block A-18 but also Block B-17 and B-19.
The authority is a statutory body with exclusive rights to explore petroleum resources in the Joint Development Area of Malaysia and Thailand.
